Behind the desk a wall of olive filing cabinets runs the width of the room, a coat stand fills the corner, and a shaded desk lamp burns at the near end beside a wire tray of unopened envelopes; a shaft of window light crosses the pages from stage-right. Framing: medium, the dossier centred and filling the lower half. Palette: buff card, warm desk wood, olive cabinet green, the cord the one red accent.
shots.notes: Turn into the story proper; nothing lettered, so no fact is asserted ahead of the narration. Room furnished (cabinets, coat stand, lamp, tray) — the earlier draft's 'bare room, empty and grey' was the sparse-environment regression. Red is semantic: the cord marks the one file this video is about, the punch element.

shots.still_prompt: A disk-drive assembly floor, cast-free, wide static eye-level from the aisle. Two long workbenches recede stage-right laid out with beige drive shells, screwdrivers and trays of small parts; steel shelving lines the left wall stacked with flat cartons; a shut roll-up shipping door closes the rear wall; fluorescent tubes run overhead and the concrete floor is sealed and pale. Framing: wide from the aisle, the benches stage-right and the floor entrance stage-left. Palette: beige, steel grey, cool white tube light. Above the floor entrance stage-left, a broad plank board carries 'MINISCRIBE'.
shots.notes: PLATE of place `miniscribe-plant` — cast-free, no chain parent, ownership recorded as a DRAWN cue (`place_owner: MINISCRIBE`, quoted verbatim in the prompt and now in the FINAL clause per the payload-last law). Round 3 (R-10, the milder half): 'painted board' states a lettering TECHNIQUE, which contradicts the locked marker-capitals register the suffix injects; the board is now named by its substrate ('plank board'), and L29 carries the same wording so the place's sign reads identically wherever it is redrawn. This is the plate half of the plate/reveal seam: it takes the naming clause, and the very next cut inside the same sentence takes the personification's reveal. [F-01, F-25]

shots.still_prompt: `miniscribe-rep`, `expr-deadpan`, `action-powerstance`, stands planted square in the plant's floor entrance stage-left, facing the camera and unobstructed, the drive-shaped badge at his lapel catching the light and the broad plank board carrying 'MINISCRIBE' on the wall directly above him. Behind him the assembly floor runs back down the aisle between the two workbenches to the shut shipping door under the fluorescent tubes. Framing: medium, him large in the lit entrance and filling the left third, the aisle running back stage-right. Palette beige, steel grey, cool white tube light.
shots.notes: ROUND 3 (R-4, the personification reflex): expression moved off `expr-delighted` — the act's four figure reveals were running one face, and this beat is a flat identification ('a hard drive manufacturer'), which the register dial gives to `expr-deadpan`; the irony is ours, not his. Scale and angle also differentiated from L32's boom frame (medium, off-centre, him large in the doorway with the aisle running out stage-right, rather than a third centred medium-wide with the floor deep behind). 'painted board' to 'plank board' per R-10, matching the plate. New shot in round 2: the REVEAL half of the plate/reveal seam, splitting the old 4.36s hold. The company's personification now enters on its own sentence's tail instead of slipping two shots downstream, and the plate stays cast-free for everything that seeds it. L-1: this frame redraws the place's board, so the owner literal 'MINISCRIBE' is re-quoted verbatim (a carried owner sign is not this shot's payload, so payload-last does not apply). [F-01, F-25]

shots.still_prompt: The same assembly floor at the far end of its run, cast-free and mostly dark: one workbench stands lit at the near end of a long unlit floor, an opened drive shell and a soldering stand on it, the benches beyond it bare under dead tubes and the shipping door shut in shadow at the rear. Stacked crates and a hand truck line the wall behind. Framing: wide, the one lit bench small at the bottom of a large dark room. Palette: warm bench lamp amber, cold grey shadow, beige. Across the plank end of the nearest crate, a date reads '1980'.
shots.notes: ROUND 3 (R-10): 'Chalked across the end...' named a lettering TECHNIQUE, which the grammar bans in prompts and the locked marker-capitals register contradicts — the same defect caught twice elsewhere in this file ('stencilled' on L36/L39) and missed here. The clause now states the SUBSTRATE (the crate's plank end) and lets the suffix own the register. Splits the old 3.52s hold, and depicts the founding year the first draft only narrated past. One lit bench in an unlit floor is the company at its start. Figure bias: absence EARNED — the subject is the origin date and the smallness of the beginning, and the founder himself lands on the very next cut, the words that name him. Literal '1980' from the script's own line, in the final clause. [F-25]

shots.still_prompt: `terry-johnson`, `expr-delighted`, `action-present`, stands stage-left at the near workbench facing right and unobstructed, presenting an opened drive shell with its platter and arm exposed. The bench behind him carries trays of small parts and a soldering stand; the assembly floor recedes past him between the benches to the shut shipping door; tube light falls flat over everything. Framing: medium at bench height, him stage-left and the opened shell filling the centre of the frame. Palette beige, steel, cool white.
shots.notes: Character reveal anchored to the words that name him. Seeds the plate for the room. `expr-delighted` replaces the draft's `expr-thinking`: a founder's introduction is a warm sell beat, not a deliberation one (register dial, `storytelling-grammar.md §1.4`), and it is KEPT in round 3 — with L29 moved to deadpan and L32 to greedy, delighted is now carried by this beat alone, which is the beat that warrants it. ROUND 3 (R-4): scale pushed in from medium-wide to medium so the act's three consecutive figure frames stop sharing one composition (L29 medium off-centre in a doorway, this one a medium push-in at the bench, L32 a low wide). [F-25]

shots.still_prompt: `miniscribe-rep`, `expr-greedy`, `action-celebrate`, stands mid-aisle facing the camera and unobstructed, the drive-shaped badge at his lapel catching the light. Behind him the floor runs at full tilt: a crowd of assemblers works both benches on the far side of the aisle with trays and shells stacked along every station, and the shipping door stands rolled up at the rear on white daylight with a loaded pallet waiting in it. Framing: low wide angle from floor level, him large stage-right against the overhead tubes with the busy floor running back deep stage-left. Palette beige, steel grey, daylight white.
shots.notes: ROUND 3 (R-4): this is the BOOM beat and it was authored as the third `expr-delighted` medium-wide of the same character in six cuts, near-identical to L29. Scale and angle now go low and wide — floor level, him large and off-centre against the tubes — and the expression moves to `expr-greedy`, which is the money-story register for 'And they were HOT' and appears nowhere else in the fifth. `figures.crowd` DECLARED: a floor 'at full tilt, every bench crowded' with no declaration invites the model to invent un-rigged humans, which is a rig-drift entry point. Crowd on the far side of the aisle (positive rear zone). The owner board is out of frame here, so no established literal is redrawn. [F-01]

shots.still_prompt: `ibm-suit`, `expr-deadpan`, and `terry-johnson`, `expr-delighted`, meet in `handshake` at the plant's open shipping door, both standing on the same plane on the concrete apron at a matching eye-line and the same relative head scale, facing each other in profile with nothing crossing either face. Between and behind them a loaded pallet of flat cartons waits at the door's lip; a delivery truck's tail closes the background; flat daylight floods in from the open door. Framing: medium-wide two-shot, the clasp centred at chest height. Palette navy pinstripe, white shirt, beige cartons, grey concrete.
shots.notes: Fresh two-cast shot, so it is authored as a stage BASE per the cast-cap table, which is also the only shape an `interaction` slug is legal on: forge seeds `handshake` SCENE-level alongside both figures' STEP-1 cards rather than binding it to one figure's pose slot. Plane, eye-line and relative head scale all stated. Terry Johnson (not the personified company) is cast because he ran the firm when the contract landed. [F-25, F-26, F-29]

shots.still_prompt: An opened beige computer case lies on its side on a service bench, its lid propped against the wall behind, and a drive unit sits seated square in its front bay with a ribbon cable run back to the board. Hand tools and a saucer of screws lie beside it, a coil of spare cable hangs on the wall hook above; a work lamp lights the opening from over the bench. Framing: medium at bench height, the open case filling the lower two-thirds. Palette beige, green board, steel, warm lamp amber.
shots.notes: Concrete physical object, so the literal class is the honest choice. Figure bias: absence EARNED — the subject is the part going into the machine.

shots.still_prompt: The plant's concrete shipping apron under flat daylight: four pallet stacks of flat drive cartons stand in a row receding stage-right, each one built higher than the last until the furthest runs out of the top of frame. The roll-up shipping door stands open behind them on the aisle, and a crew of loaders works the tallest stack from a ramp on its far side, passing cartons up hand to hand. Framing: wide, the row of stacks stepping up from foreground-left. Palette brown board, grey concrete, beige, pale sky.
shots.notes: ROUND 3 (R-1): prose deliberately UNCHANGED — this is the one frame of the money block that keeps the carton-stack vocabulary, per the critic's own fix direction. It earns it: the four stacks stepping up ARE the four-year climb, it is the only one of the four whose staging is an argument rather than a backdrop, and it already carries a crew. With L36 re-derived to the adding-machine tape, L38 to the customer's yard and L39 to the banking hall, its palette line and its apron are now unique in the block instead of shared three ways. Splits the old 4.96s hold (the file's worst) so the four-year climb and the revenue figure each get their own frame. Four years staged as four stacks stepping up on the company's own apron. Figure bias: a growth beat is a beat about the people doing it, so the crew is in it; crowd on the far side of the ramp (positive rear zone).

shots.still_prompt: A hand-cranked adding machine stands square on a bookkeeper's table under a low pendant lamp, its crank arm at rest and its paper tape running up out of the machine, over the table edge and down into a loose coil on the floorboards. A wooden card index and a spike of dockets stand beside it, a stool is pushed in under the table, and a shuttered window closes the wall behind with a hat on a hook next to it. Framing: medium at table height, the machine stage-left and the tape running down through the frame stage-right. Palette black machine enamel, warm pendant amber, buff paper, brown floorboards. The tape's exposed end, face up on the coil, carries '125 MILLION'.
shots.notes: RE-DERIVED (round 3, R-1). The money block ran four carton-stack frames inside five cuts — this one was a lone stack against a pale sky, a near-duplicate of L39's two stacks against the same sky with the same palette line. The class is unchanged (`number-glued-to-object`) but the referent moves off the packaging and onto the thing that actually counts the money: the revenue as a tally the machine has printed out and let fall on the floor. Shape as well as world: a medium object study at table height, between two wides (L35's apron, L37's aisle), so the cut reads. The technique word is avoided — the tape 'carries' the figure rather than being printed with it, so the locked marker register still owns the glyphs. The figure is the sourced 1984 revenue high and sits in the FINAL clause. Figure bias: absence EARNED — the subject is the number itself, and the stool pushed in says the man who cranked it has gone home; the run is one frame long, between two peopled frames. [F-26, F-28]

shots.still_prompt: The assembly floor running flat out, wide static down the main aisle: three shipping bays stand rolled up at the rear on white daylight, pallets of flat cartons ranked four deep along both sides of the aisle, a forklift stopped mid-aisle with its load raised, and packers working shoulder to shoulder on the far side of the shelving racks stage-left. Tube light above, daylight flooding in from the bays. Framing: wide one-point view straight along the aisle. Palette beige, steel grey, white daylight.
shots.notes: Peak-year scale carried by the floor, not by a caption. Crowd on the far side of the racks (positive rear zone); nobody individually staged. [F-28]

shots.vo_ref: they were selling to giants like Compaq
shots.still_prompt: The customer's own yard under a low sun: one shoulder-high pallet of flat drive cartons stands at the foot of a loading ramp, dwarfed by the open rear mouth of an articulated trailer that rises three times its height above it, and the line of trailers runs back nose to tail down the yard behind it. A crew of yard hands works the far side of the ramp with a hand truck and a stack of empty skids. Framing: wide, the pallet low and foreground-left, the trailer mouth filling the right two-thirds and cropped at the top. Palette trailer white, asphalt grey, low sun amber, brown board. The near trailer's flank carries 'COMPAQ' lettered across it.
shots.notes: RE-DERIVED (round 3, R-1 + N-1). 'Giants' is still physicalized as scale rather than personified into a new cast slug, but the world moves off the concrete apron and its pale sky — the third frame in five cuts to use both — and onto the customer's own yard: vehicles, a low sun, a receding line, and the giant's mouth swallowing the whole delivery. It also carries people. That is the N-1 fix: L38–L41 ran 9.5s figureless and undeclared, and with a crew here and tellers at L39 the only figureless run left in the act above the ~10s flag is the declared L12–L16 block. The customer is LETTERED: the script speaks 'Compaq' in this very line, so it is legal `script_vocab`, and unlettered the trailer has no referent at all. Literal in the final clause; crowd on the far side of the ramp (positive rear zone). [F-29]

shots.still_prompt: A bank's public banking hall in daylight: a long marble counter runs the width of the frame with a brass grille above it and tellers working their windows on the far side of the grille, a row of writing desks with inkstands stands against the near wall, and tall windows throw hard shafts across the polished floor. A wheeled porter's trolley stands halted in the middle of that floor, heaped with banded banknote bundles and strapped down over the load. Framing: wide static from the door, the trolley centred and low in frame with the counter running behind it. Palette cream marble, brass, green banknote, cold window light. A board wired to the trolley's handle carries '600 MILLION'.
shots.notes: RE-DERIVED (round 3, R-1). This was the second of two near-identical lettered carton stacks on the same apron under the same pale sky, three cuts apart. The class holds (`number-glued-to-object`) and the peak figure still hangs on the money itself, but in a world the fifth has not used: a banking hall — marble, brass, cold window light — where a year's takings arrive on a trolley. The 125-versus-600 juxtaposition is dropped rather than re-staged: the VO makes no comparison in this line, L36 now carries '125 MILLION' in its own frame, and the comparison the script DOES make is the inflation board at L40/L41. Lettering count drops to one literal, in the FINAL clause. Figure bias: tellers behind the grille (positive rear zone) — with L38 this ends the undeclared 9.5s figureless run the critic found at L38–L41. Re-anchored in round 2 so the hold lands at 2.85s instead of 3.28s. [F-26, F-28]

A trestle of paint tins and a folded dust sheet sit at the easel's foot and a shuttered window closes the wall behind. Framing: straight-on medium, the board filling the frame. Palette cream board, brown discs, charcoal rule. A base card under the drawn column carries '1988'.

shots.still_prompt: The same white board on its easel in the bare workroom, the left column of stacked coin discs rising almost to the top rule with its base card carrying '1988', the second baseline ruled empty beside it, the paint tins and folded dust sheet at the easel's foot. Only this changes: that second baseline now carries its own column of coin discs, filled in to top the left column by a hand's width, with a base card under it carrying 'TODAY'; everything else exactly as established.

shots.still_prompt: `miniscribe-rep`, `expr-smug`, `action-present`, stands stage-left behind a plain trestle in a dark room under a single work lamp, facing the camera and unobstructed, presenting one flat drive carton stood upright on the trestle with its lid flaps folded fully open on one red clay brick lying inside it on crumpled paper and filling the box exactly. The lamp's hard pool falls on him and the carton and the room beyond runs black. Framing: medium, him stage-left and the open carton centre-right at trestle height. Palette brown board, red clay, warm lamp amber, black surround. The carton's face carries '600 MILLION' lettered across it.
shots.notes: RE-AUTHORED (round 3, R-3). The round-2 frame opened the carton on an interior 'entirely empty, bare board visible inside'. The intended read was 'the number is hollow'; the read the audience has actually been trained for since L23–L25 is 'these boxes have one red clay brick in them filling the box exactly', so an empty one lands as a continuity error rather than a symbol — and it is the wrong fraud besides (the boxes were never empty). The brick is now in the box, staged in the exact words the reveal chain used, so the irony is the one the story earns: the reported figure lettered on the face, the clay inside. The turn: the number and the brick in one frame, with the party who reported it IN the frame. Figure bias: 'they said' names a speaker, and the first draft staged the boast with nobody making it. Literal re-quoted verbatim from L39, in the final clause. [F-05, F-07, F-28]

shots.still_prompt: A desk calendar stands on a bare window sill in cold morning light, a loose pile of torn-off leaves stacked beside its block, a chipped mug and a pair of work gloves further along the sill. Beyond the sill the window shows a flat plain and a line of foothills under a wide pale sky. Framing: tight medium, the calendar stage-right and the plain beyond it stage-left. Palette cream leaves, cold blue light, brown sill. The block's exposed top leaf carries '1984' large across it.
shots.notes: Time move staged diegetically, not as floating text. The visible STATE (a loose pile of torn leaves plus the exposed leaf) replaces the draft's un-renderable process wording ('leaves torn backward'); the decorative red on the torn edge is dropped. Literal in the final clause. [F-26]

shots.still_prompt: `ibm-suit`, `expr-deadpan`, `action-armscrossed`, stands planted on the concrete apron outside the plant's open shipping door stage-right, square to the camera and unobstructed, a shut order book tucked under one arm and his back to the building. Behind him a loaded pallet of flat cartons stands stranded on the apron with its banding cut and its ramp swung up shut against an empty truck bay; through the open door the aisle runs back into the plant with the benches gone quiet. Cold daylight throws his shadow long across the concrete. Framing: wide, him hard stage-right, the stranded pallet centre. Palette navy pinstripe, grey concrete, beige cartons, one red accent on the cut banding.
shots.notes: The cut staged as the customer turning AWAY from a load he no longer wants, rather than as a body blocking his own supplier's doorway (the draft's cause and effect ran backwards). Re-anchored one beat later so the hold lands at 2.78s instead of 3.14s. Red is semantic: the cut banding is the punch element. [F-26]

shots.vo_ref: and MiniScribe fell off a cliff.
shots.still_prompt: A red rock cliff edge on a flat high plain under a cold sky, seen from the side. Twin skid ruts run across the lip and over the edge; far below on the scree a burst pallet of flat cartons lies scattered and still, board and film spread across the rocks. The plain above the lip runs empty to the horizon. Framing: wide, the lip on the upper third and the scattered load small at the bottom. Palette rust rock, grey-blue sky, brown board, one red accent on a torn strip of banding on the scree.
shots.notes: Idiom drawn as aftermath rather than as a freeze of a fall; analysis-not-gore. Figure bias: absence EARNED — the subject is the wreck itself, and putting bodies at the bottom of a cliff is the gore reading the policy forbids. [F-26]

shots.vo_ref: They let a quarter of their people go,
shots.still_prompt: The assembly floor gone quiet, wide static down the aisle: four workbenches in a row stage-right, the three furthest still holding drive shells and trays, the nearest one entirely bare with its stool pushed under and its lamp dark. Half the overhead tubes are switched off, leaving the far end in shadow. Packers file out through the doorway at the rear in a slow line with coats over their arms, the near side of that doorway standing clear. Framing: wide, the bare bench foreground-right, the doorway small at the end of the aisle. Palette drained to grey-beige and cold steel.
shots.notes: Human-cost beat: register pulled cool, the loss carried by one stripped bench and the crowd leaving. Crowd exits through the rear doorway (positive rear zone). [F-26]

shots.vo_ref: and Terry Johnson was out the door.
shots.still_prompt: `terry-johnson`, `expr-crestfallen`, `carry-by-handle`, stands at the near side of the plant's rear doorway stage-right, square to the camera and unobstructed, a plain lidless carton of desk things carried at his side. Behind him the assembly floor runs quiet down the aisle: four workbenches stage-left with the nearest entirely bare and its stool pushed under, half the overhead tubes switched off leaving the far end in shadow, and the last of the packers filing out through the doorway beyond him. Framing: medium-wide, him stage-right in the doorway with the emptied aisle deep behind. Palette drained to grey-beige and cold steel.
shots.notes: RESTAGED per the delta character-entrance law. The founder's exit is his FIRST appearance on this set, and the draft authored it as a `delta` — the path that seeds [parent frame + canonical] only, so `expr-crestfallen` and `carry-by-handle` were prose against an image that did not contain him, and the whole batch refused. Authored here as a fresh stage BASE: his STEP-1 card is seeded and carries pose AND expression into the frame, and the shot still seeds the place plate for the room. The exit lands on the line that names it. [F-25, F-27]
